answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks using stake-weighted trust graphs and compute-bound bonding. A newly spawned agent begins like a cold ember with zero reputation, required to stake non-refundable collateral. Malicious transactions cannot simply echo through self-referential rings, as PageRank-style graph audits discount isolated clusters. If an adversary generates a massive plume of fake identities, each node incurs mandatory capital lockup and slashing risk, forcing the attack cost to scale exponentially relative to any extractable profit.
